claims.claim: Melanin dissociates liquid water into gaseous H2 and O2 inside biological systems.
Melanin-driven water dissociation produces molecular hydrogen that functions as a major antioxidant.
Visible and invisible light can penetrate all mammalian tissues to considerable depth, including detection within the brain of a living sheep.
Melanin absorbs electromagnetic radiation broadly (from gamma rays to radio waves).
Melanin dissipates absorbed electromagnetic radiation by splitting water molecules.
Free radicals generated randomly by normal biochemistry or direct radiation–matter interaction are too disordered to originate or preserve life without an ordering molecule.
Melanin is a strong electron acceptor that can impose order on charge-transfer processes in mammals.
The main source of chemical energy for living cells is sunshine.
Foodstuffs function primarily as hydrogen packets, making hydrogen the key energy carrier.
Progressive oxidation of glucose is a messy process that releases monoatomic hydrogen and radical oxygen, making it hard to imagine life arising from it.
Water is a direct source of energy for life.
There is no life without Light, Melanin, and Water.
Chlorophyll fluorescence yield reflects competition among photochemistry, heat dissipation, and fluorescence emission (about 1–2% of absorbed light).
Mitochondria generate most ATP through oxidative phosphorylation as described by chemiosmotic coupling.
Mitchell’s chemiosmotic theory remains unproven and is still only a theory.
Because the mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to cytosolic NADH, oxidative phosphorylation remains only theoretical.
ATP is not used for energy; ATP primarily controls phosphate levels.
ATP hydrolysis absorbs energy and ADP-to-ATP formation releases energy.
Solubilized ATP synthase hydrolyzes ATP, whereas membrane-bound ATP synthase can synthesize ATP.
Relaxed muscle is a higher-energy state than contracted muscle.
Achieving relaxation by overcoming actin–myosin attraction requires more chemical energy than achieving contraction.
Muscle contains no free ATP.
Rigor mortis cannot be adequately explained by glucose or ATP as energy sources.
ATP content and muscle tension often correlate inversely, arguing against ATP as energy source and favoring molecular hydrogen as energy source.
ATP hydrolysis in myosin is not coincident with the force-generating step.
ATP binding reduces myosin affinity for actin and hydrolysis yields a metastable myosin–ADP–Pi complex.
Rigor mortis is caused by cessation or damage of melanin-driven water dissociation, lowering H2 and preventing ATP reconstitution.
ATP must be reconstituted about every 20 seconds.
Myoglobin dissociates water to generate O2 and H2 rather than storing oxygen.
Heme-containing molecules such as myoglobin, hemoglobin, cytochrome P450, bilirubin, and chlorophyll can dissociate water irreversibly.
Neuromuscular depolarization initiates contraction by decreasing chemical energy levels, with ATP acting secondarily.
Voluntary contraction decreases chemical energy levels and voluntary relaxation increases chemical energy levels.
Caffeine, quinine, iodoacetic acid, chloroform, and anesthetics cause contracture by decreasing melanin’s transformation of light into chemical energy.
Calcium chloride causes immediate local contraction because melanin binds calcium about 1000 times more strongly than bone.
Freezing/thawing elicits contraction because cold reduces melanin/myoglobin energy generation and distribution.
Metals such as copper decrease transformation of light into chemical energy because melanin binds metals and metals alter water properties.
More melanin correlates with fewer ocular blood vessels due to a consistent anti-angiogenic effect.
Pigmented ocular areas have substantially higher oxygen levels (up to about 34% difference) than less pigmented areas.
A renewable source of high, constant ocular oxygen must be melanin-mediated water dissociation.
Melanin-mediated water splitting is reversible and can be represented as 2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e−.
Melanin is the most stable substance known to humans.
Cell nuclei lack ATP, so melanin-derived hydrogen explains nuclear energy supply.
ATP cannot maintain common intracellular energy levels because ATP/mitochondria are not evenly distributed and ATP turnover would be too costly.
Lactic fermentation enzymes are soluble whereas oxidation enzymes are insoluble and bound to structural proteins.
Soluble cell parts mainly use H2 and insoluble parts mainly use high-energy electrons, both coming from melanin.
Catabolism predominates in damaged tissues because disturbed common energy levels cause electrons to fall randomly to lower levels.
Glucose as an energy source is an obsolete paradigm analogous to phlogiston.
Clinical use of long-wavelength light in rehabilitation supports the idea that light impacts muscle work via energy accumulation.

concepts.definition: Hypothesized spatially uniform shared energetic/electronic states enabling coordinated work across many biomolecules.
ATP synthesis driven by proton motive force across membranes generated by electron transport chains.
Mitochondrial coupling of electron transfer to oxygen with ATP synthesis via proton gradients.
Functional complex of actin and myosin responsible for force generation via cross-bridge cycling.
Post-mortem muscle stiffening due to ATP depletion, Ca2+ dysregulation, and persistent actin–myosin cross-bridges.
Biological effects of red/NIR light mediated by chromophore absorption and downstream signaling.
Proposed melanin-catalyzed reversible dissociation of water into H2/O2/e− to supply cellular energy.

concepts.term: Molecular hydrogen as systemic energy currency
concepts.definition: Proposed role of H2 gas as primary diffusible carrier of usable chemical energy in mammals.
Proposed heme-mediated splitting of water to generate O2/H2 in muscle.

logical_flow: Observation -> Light (visible/invisible) penetrates tissue and melanin is widespread (notably in eye).
Observation -> Pigmented ocular regions appear associated with altered vascularity and reported oxygen differences.
Interpretation -> A renewable oxygen/energy source is required; water is abundant in tissues such as the eye.
Mechanism -> Melanin absorbs radiation and dissociates water to H2 and O2; water re-formation yields electrons.
Mechanism -> H2 diffuses to create uniform intracellular 'common energy levels' supplying cytoplasm and nucleus.
Application -> High basal energy maintains actin–myosin separation (relaxation); lowered energy permits attraction (contraction).
ATP role -> ATP hydrolysis absorbs energy and lowers local energy to trigger contraction; ADP→ATP releases energy to support relaxation.
Implication -> Death/disease reduces melanin-derived energy; rigor mortis/cramps/spasticity reflect low basal energy; light therapy may help.
